{{Short description|Models the mean time to failure of a semiconductor circuit due to electromigration}}
'''Black's equation''' is a mathematical model for the [[Mean time between failures|mean time to failure]] (MTTF) of a semiconductor circuit due to [[electromigration]]: a phenomenon of [[molecule|molecular]] rearrangement (movement) in the [[solid phase]] caused by an [[electromagnetic field]]. It was first published by J. R. Black in 1969.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Black |first=J.R. |date=1969 |title=Electromigration&#8212;A brief survey and some recent results |journal=IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices |volume=16 |issue=4 |pages=338–347 |doi=10.1109/T-ED.1969.16754 |bibcode=1969ITED...16..338B |issn=0018-9383}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Rost |first=Tim |chapter=Preface |date=2005 |title=2005 IEEE International Reliability Physics Symposium, 2005. Proceedings. 43rd Annual |pages=iii–iv |doi=10.1109/RELPHY.2005.1493049|bibcode=2005relp.conf....5. |isbn=0-7803-8803-8 }}</ref>

The equation is:<ref>
R. L. de Orio.
[http://www.iue.tuwien.ac.at/phd/orio/node16.html Dissertation: "Electromigration Modeling and Simulation"].
2010.
R.L. de Orio, H. Ceric, [[Siegfried Selberherr|S. Selberherr]].
[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220456802_Physically_based_models_of_electromigration_From_Black's_equation_to_modern_TCAD_models/file/d912f50f5ceeeb4bb4.pdf "Physically based models of electromigration: From Black’s equation to modern TCAD models"]
Microelectronics Reliability journal.
2010.
</ref>
: <math>\mathrm{MTTF} = \frac{A}{j^{n}} e^\left(\frac{Q}{kT}\right)</math>
where
* <math>A</math> is a constant
* <math>j</math> is the [[current density]]
* <math>n</math> is a model parameter
* <math>Q</math> is the [[activation energy]]
* <math>k</math> is the [[Boltzmann constant]]
* <math>T</math> is the [[absolute temperature]]

The model is abstract, not based on a specific physical model, but flexibly describes the failure rate dependence on the temperature, the electrical stress, and the specific technology and materials. More adequately described as descriptive than prescriptive, the values for ''A'', ''n'', and ''Q'' are found by fitting the model to experimental data.

The model's value is that it maps experimental data taken at elevated temperature and electrical stress levels in short periods of time to expected component failure rates under actual operating conditions. Experimental data is obtained by running a combination of [[high temperature operating life]] (HTOL), electrical, and any other relevant operating environment variables.
